text: Keep the dependency direction host -> engine <- command modules, with the host abstraction (`PSHost`) as the only UI contract.

Split the engine into separately packaged components (language core, runtime, remoting, formatting, help) so enterprise deployments can omit unneeded subsystems and shrink the attack surface; the observable language behavior stays unchanged.
Provide a one-call embedding entry that takes an initial session state (as `ConsoleShell.Start` does).
Build with standard `dotnet` tooling and MSBuild props only, with version computed from one tag plus an explicit override, instead of an orchestration module needing an installed shell.

Keep the two preprocessor families (`UNIX`/`CORECLR`) out of the language core by isolating platform code behind an interface; PowerShell's use of `IsWindows` to drive `DefineConstants` spreads `#if UNIX` through the engine.
Pin a single package feed and commit lock files; PowerShell pins one feed but ships no lock files.
Generate resource accessors and type catalogs at build time with small console tools that are themselves part of the repository (`ResGen`, `TypeCatalogGen`).
Use declarative pipeline templates plus a thin script layer; keep package-format code behind a single `Start-Package`-style entry with a closed format list as `Start-PSPackage` does.
Pin third-party workflows by commit SHA and run dependency review, CodeQL and Scorecard on every change.
Validate signed payloads against an explicit allow-list signer policy before publishing.
Adopt warnings-as-errors with an explicit analyzer severity file from day one.
Write the breaking-change contract before the first release and apply it to language behavior, cmdlet parameters and protocols alike.
Keep platform differences behind interfaces rather than `#if` blocks across the engine (PowerShell has `UNIX` in 122 files).
Use the hot-path rules (no LINQ, no `params`, pre-sized collections) only inside the interpreter and runtime core, and let a profiler decide elsewhere.
Keep the four hooks (begin, process, end, stop) plus clean, with `Stopping` checked on every write.
Separate typed streams with per-stream action preferences and the Ignore / SilentlyContinue / Continue / Inquire / Stop semantics.
`ShouldProcess` decision order (remembered answer → what-if → impact threshold → prompt).
Make write permission a capability object passed to the cmdlet for the duration of a phase instead of three mutable fields on the pipeline processor checked against the current thread.
Split the 3,800-line runtime into stream writers (one per stream) behind one interface, keeping behavior identical.
Do not carry transaction support (`-UseTransaction`, `SupportsTransactions`, the engine protection scope) into the new shell; the feature is Windows-only and out of core scope. DEV: DEV-CMDLET-135.
Resolution order alias → function → cmdlet → path/file, with module-qualified names bypassing precedence; it is observable language behavior.
Make the searcher a resumable enumerator so `Get-Command`-style wildcard queries share the code with single lookups.
Keep the lookup events (pre, not-found, post) but give them typed results and a re-entrancy guard in the type system instead of a name→set dictionary of strings.
Visibility and trust-level filtering belong in the lookup, not only at run time.

Replace module auto-discovery by file analysis on every unknown name with an explicit, signed command index that is refreshed on module install/update; keep module-qualified auto-load. DEV: DEV-DISC-120.

Do not implement the `Legacy` native-argument passing style (string re-quoting) or the name-based legacy-program list; offer only list-based passing (`Standard`) and a per-command opt-in for programs that need a raw command line. DEV: DEV-DISC-121.

Start the child process after all begin phases (or make the start point explicit) so pipeline ordering is the same for cmdlets and programs; keep the "console-direct when last into the default output" optimization.
`$LASTEXITCODE` set on every native exit; error-on-non-zero as an opt-in preference.
Sequence points with per-function bit arrays and a single hook called only in debug mode.
Three breakpoint kinds (line, command, variable) with action blocks, and the five resume actions.
Expose the debugger through a protocol-neutral interface suited to an external adapter (the Debug Adapter Protocol), keeping the prompt commands for terminals.
Debugger attach/enable is a policy-controlled, audited privilege, and the prompt runs under the lowest trust level present on the stack. DEV: DEV-DBG-195.
Do not port nested debugging of jobs and remote runspaces (`DebugJob`, `Embedded/StandaloneRunspaceDebugger`) in the first version. DEV: DEV-DBG-196.
Split errors into records (non-terminating, streamed) and exceptions (terminating), with the `ErrorAction` decision list; it defines script behavior.
Statement-level guard with continue-by-default and `throw` as the always-terminating form; keep traps with `continue`/`break` semantics.
`$Error` as a bounded, newest-first, de-duplicated history; `$?` as a read-only all-scope variable.
Keep `ErrorRecord` fields and the 32 categories but add a schema version, a correlation id and a redaction marker for sensitive fields.
Make the `$Error` capacity configurable (the source hard-codes 256 and no preference variable controls it).
Native exit codes in `$LASTEXITCODE` and `$?`, error on non-zero only by preference.
Separate the audit stream (policy decisions, denials) from the user error stream so that `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` or `Ignore` can never suppress an audit record. DEV: DEV-ERR-180.
Source-identifier based events with queue, actions, auto-unregister and reserved engine identifiers.
Run actions serially at idle points in the subscriber's session state.
Replace `Reflection.Emit` handler generation with expression-tree or `Delegate.CreateDelegate` adapters (or `DynamicInvoke` fallback) so the feature works where dynamic assemblies are blocked.
Bound the received-event queue and action queue with policy-defined limits and drop/oldest rules. DEV: DEV-EVT-198.
Do not port forwarded events (`PSRemoteEventManager`) or the WMI/CIM event sources in the first version. DEV: DEV-EVT-199.
One interpreter context object holding the current session state, strict mode, preference lookup and error state; pass it to runtime helpers instead of using globals.
Resolve preference variables through the normal variable lookup with a typed fallback.
Guard recursion with a stack-depth check that raises a dedicated "script call depth" error.
Leave out language modes and binder-cache invalidation unless a restricted mode is added later.
Keep the member resolution order instance → type data → adapter → base with the five reserved names; scripts depend on it.
Merge type data from the least to the most specific type name, with member-set inheritance.
Select adapters by type with inheritance (nearest registered base type wins) instead of exact full-name match, as the source comment itself proposes.
Make adapter and type-table registries per-runspace (or per-session-state) objects rather than static caches, so one session cannot change another's member view.
Bind script members to the definer's language mode and keep deserialized objects data-only.
Do not carry the WMI, DirectoryEntry, DataRow/DataRowView and COM adapters into the first version; keep .NET, XML, `PSObject`, member-set and the third-party adapter bridge. DEV: DEV-ETS-150.

Compile the built-in type data to a table at build time (as PowerShell does) but also publish it as a versioned data file, so tooling and a clean-room implementation share one source. DEV: DEV-ETS-151.
Two-stage output: objects → formatting records (data) → line layout, with the record state machine; `Format-*` output can be piped to `Out-*`.
View selection by type-name list with perfect match then best match, then property-count fallback (table at or below the threshold, else list).
Replace the hidden sub-pipeline (`CommandWrapper` over `Out-LineOutput`) by a direct call to the formatter and sink objects, keeping the same observable output.
Keep table width auto-sizing but make the buffering window a configurable policy (count and time) instead of the fixed 300 ms.
Provide an optional structured output sink (typed records for machines) next to the text sink, so enterprise tooling does not parse text. DEV: DEV-FMT-160.

Do not carry the format XML loader family (`typeDataXmlLoader*`, schema validation) in the first version; ship built-in views as compiled data plus a small JSON/YAML view definition for extensions. DEV: DEV-FMT-161.
Comment-based help with the keyword set above and `.EXTERNALHELP`/forwarding, since scripts written for PowerShell carry it.
Replace the fixed provider list with registered providers that declare category and priority, keeping the same default order.
Keep forwarding but make cycles a static check at load rather than a run-time exception.
Deliver updatable help as signed packages with a catalog and an offline mode, verified before install. DEV: DEV-HELP-165.
Do not port MAML as the authoring format or the DSC resource provider; use a lighter structured format (and the comment-based format) for built-in help. DEV: DEV-HELP-166.
One `Job` abstraction with child jobs, per-stream collections, finished-state semantics and a state-changed event.
`ForEach-Object -Parallel` semantics: throttle default 5, `$using:` capture, completion-order output, timeout.
Add an explicit transition table to the job state machine (the source accepts any transition).
Child processes and parallel runspaces inherit policy, language mode and visibility from the parent as a hard rule, plus per-job quotas. DEV: DEV-JOB-190.
Do not port `ThrottlingJob`, `ContainerParentJob` and the job source-adapter registry in the first version; one local job type plus the parallel pool suffices. DEV: DEV-JOB-191.
Module = folder + manifest + optional root script/binary, with per-module session state and an export list; manifest is data, not code.
Version-folder rule (folder version equals manifest version) and constraint matching with required/minimum/maximum.
Export engine with wildcard patterns per category and manifest lists overriding script exports.
Keep the exported-command analysis cache but make it a versioned, signed, explicitly refreshed index (see DEV-DISC-120), validated by content hash rather than last write time.
Module search path entries carry trust levels, and auto-load applies only from trusted entries unless policy allows more. DEV: DEV-MOD-170.
Split the 7,500-line loader class by responsibility: path resolution, manifest reader, module factory per kind, export engine, importer, remover.
Do not implement Windows PowerShell compatibility imports (`ImportModulesUsingWinCompat`), `.cdxml` CIM modules or DSC resource exports in the first version. DEV: DEV-MOD-171.
Keep the binding order (named → positional → defaults → dynamic → remaining → mandatory → pipeline) and the exact → coerced two-pass for positional and pipeline binding; it is observable.
Parameter sets as bit masks with a default set and the ambiguity-by-mandatory tie-break.
Unambiguous-prefix parameter names including aliases; exact match wins.
Lift the 32-set limit by using a set-index bit vector type, keeping the same semantics.
Factor the "default binding in use → elaborate error" pattern into one wrapper, and the binding steps into an explicit pipeline of stages with a trace result object.
Run transformation/validation callbacks under the callee's language mode; keep the explicit transition flag.
Redact bound values in execution-detail logging by parameter type and attribute instead of logging the first 256 characters of every value. DEV: DEV-BIND-130.
Keep the verb contract (item, container, navigation, content, property) as interfaces with capability flags instead of a five-level class hierarchy with context-bound state.
Drive-qualified, provider-qualified and relative path forms and per-scope drives.

Put a mandatory policy mediation layer between the engine and providers (root confinement, rights, audit) and pass an explicit per-call context object instead of mutating a `Context` field on the provider. DEV: DEV-PROV-140.
Treat variables, functions, aliases and environment as providers over session state.
Replace the all-exceptions-swallowed `ItemExists` with a typed result (exists, absent, failed) and let `Test-Path` decide.
Do not implement file-system auto-mounting of Windows volumes on lookup miss as an engine feature; mount drives explicitly or from configuration. DEV: DEV-PROV-141.
Keep the synchronous depth-first push model with a zero default buffer threshold: it defines the observable streaming behavior of pipelines.
Bind all commands, then run all begin phases in order, then process, then end in order; keep the clean phase outside the stop path.
First terminating error wins; later failures are logged, not thrown.

Keep the one-pipeline-per-runspace rule but make the state machines explicit tables with a single transition function; the original spreads transitions over several classes with events queued under locks.
Replace the fixed 10 MB thread stack plus per-call stack probe with a configurable depth limit that raises the same `ScriptCallDepth` error.

Offer a bounded, cancellable stream between host and pipeline by default (the original default is effectively unbounded) and a time/memory budget per pipeline, as an opt-in deviation. DEV: DEV-PIPE-110.
Create the policy decision point at command-processor construction and before parameter binding: command origin, language mode and session-state visibility are all known there.
Do not reproduce the "pulse pipeline" (an internal empty pipeline used to run pending engine events); schedule event processing on the runspace's own loop. DEV: DEV-PIPE-111.

Deny-by-default restricted sessions built from a declarative data file: empty baseline, named visible commands, parameter constraints, language mode, execution policy, startup scripts and transcripts.
Visibility as a per-command property (public/private) enforced at resolution and invocation, so internal helpers stay callable.
Add explicit deny rules and a defined precedence (deny over allow) to role merging, plus a "what can this role do" report. DEV: DEV-JEA-220.
Make parameter constraints part of the command contract (typed policy objects) and enforce them in the binder, instead of attribute-name keys in a hashtable.
Sign configuration and role files and verify them at load.
Do not build remoting in the first version; if built later, do not copy PSRP's XML payload design or its in-protocol key exchange. DEV: DEV-REM-210.
Keep the lesson that protocol versions are explicit and negotiated downward with a published history, and that security belongs to a mutually authenticated encrypted transport.
Keep length-prefixed fragmentation with start/end flags and a priority lane for control and prompt traffic.
Forward host calls (prompts, progress) as typed RPCs with call ids if a remote host UI is ever needed.

Keep the idea of a self-describing, depth-limited, reference-preserving interchange format with exact primitives and inert property bags for the rest, but choose a schema'd format (for example JSON or CBOR with a type vocabulary) and keep CLIXML import/export as a compatibility adapter.
Never instantiate types from payload type names; rehydrate through a fixed allow-list only.
Prohibit DTDs, cap entity expansion and nesting depth in every XML or structured reader.
Add an explicit maximum input size and a streaming limit to the primary reader, and mark sensitive properties so depth-1 bags cannot leak them. DEV: DEV-SER-215.
Keep a marker on deserialized objects (type-name prefix and flag) so formatting and policy can tell data from live objects.
Do not implement WSMan, Hyper-V socket or container transports; they are Windows-specific and tied to native components. DEV: DEV-REM-211.
If remoting is added, start with an SSH-subsystem or local-pipe transport that delegates authentication and encryption to an existing secure channel.
Local pipes bound to the creating user, single instance, remote clients rejected.
Use length-prefixed binary frames instead of Base64 XML elements on stdio, keeping acknowledgement and signal semantics.
Keep a parser-selected `Mode` (Command / Expression / TypeName / Signature) on a pull-style tokenizer; initial mode Command; each switch restored in `finally`.
Treat `-name` as a parameter in Command mode and as dash-operator-or-parameter in Expression mode; recognize keywords only in Command/Signature mode.
Reproduce the generic-token rule in Command mode: operator characters and non-terminators glue into one word, with the exact terminator set (`ForceStartNewToken`).

Implement rescan with an explicit snapshot (position + mode) instead of resyncing from a token, but keep the one-token-lookahead contract so a mode switch re-reads the peeked token. Why: same observable behavior, simpler to reason about.
Number literal grammar: suffix before multiplier, multiplier needs `b`, two's-complement hex/binary, int→long→decimal→double promotion.
Pre-scan `$(...)` inside strings with a tokenizer-aware scan (quotes and comments), not paren counting alone. Why: avoids the early-`)` edge case; observable behavior for valid scripts is identical.
Leave `#requires` processing and signature lookalike detection out of the tokenizer (move to a later phase or omit); replace with a dedicated pragma pass if the owner wants it.
Hand-written recursive descent with exactly one token of lookahead; the parser, not the tokenizer, owns Command/Expression mode and restores it after each rule.
At a statement start try an expression in Expression mode first (assignment target or first pipeline element), then fall back to a command.

Parse binary operators with an operand stack and operator stack driven by a per-operator precedence level, all left-associative; comma binds tighter than every binary operator; ternary and assignment sit above.
Do not require a terminator after block statements; skip optional newlines and semicolons between statements, and stop pipelines at newline, `;`, `)`, `}`, `&&`, `||`, `&`.

Collect errors with de-duplication, return error AST nodes and recover by pretending closers or skipping to a sync token; mark errors at end-of-script as incomplete input so the REPL can continue the line.
Keep stack-depth protection but replace the retry-on-new-thread with a fixed nesting limit that reports `ScriptTooComplicated`. Why: same observable error, deterministic and testable.
Do not perform filesystem access or runspace creation while parsing (`using assembly` resolution, `configuration`); resolve such directives in a later phase.
One class per construct, get-only properties, constructor invariants that throw on invalid combinations, and parent links set exactly once.
Provide a pre-order visitor with `Continue`/`SkipChildren`/`StopVisit` and a post-visit hook that fires on every exit path.
Keep error nodes (`ErrorStatementAst`, `ErrorExpressionAst`) that hold partially parsed children so tooling works on broken scripts.
Treat hashtable values as statements and keep `PipelineChainAst` left-nested with a plain `PipelineAst` on the right, as the parser produces them.

Use one visitor family with a default `Visit` for new nodes instead of two families gated by "v2" interfaces. Why: the v1/v2 split exists for source compatibility with external visitors, which a new shell does not have.

Make type names (`ITypeName`) plain syntax objects resolved lazily by the type system, with a cache owned by the resolver. Why: keeps the AST free of reflection state while keeping the observable `[type]` resolution.
Do not store compiler caches (`TupleIndex`, `RuntimeUsingIndex`, `TypeDefinitionAst.Type`) or assignment-code-generation methods on AST nodes; keep them in side tables keyed by node.

Provide an allow-list "literal data" evaluator (no commands, no member calls, no binary operators, node and key caps) for manifests and data sections, evaluated without the compiler. Why: same observable safety as `SafeGetValue`, without depending on the compiler for unary/convert nodes.

Keep semantic rules (duplicate parameters, loop-control placement, assignment targets, attribute-argument constants, hashtable duplicate keys, `$using` shape) as a post-parse pass that reports into the parser's error list.
Validate `data` sections with an allow-list checker and refuse operators flagged as disallowed in restricted mode.
Resolve type names in a fixed order (script types, accelerators, assemblies, user accelerators, `using namespace` retries) and cache results per (name, state).

Do slot allocation as a separate pass with a definite-assignment analysis, but start with a simple rule (slot only if assigned before every read, never for non-local scopes) and keep a dynamic-lookup fallback. Why: same observable variable behavior with far less code than the flow-graph analysis.
Report all class-definition errors in the semantic pass instead of at first compile. Why: same error set, earlier and deterministic.
Do not run module lookups (`Get-Module -ListAvailable`) while parsing `using module`; record the directive and resolve it in a later phase.

Start with a tree-walking evaluator over the AST that implements the protocols of §6 and [IR-SPEC.md](IR-SPEC.md) §5; add an IR later only if profiling demands it. Why: same observable behavior, far less code than a 6,600-line expression-tree compiler.
Implement statement output as writes to the current output pipe with temporary capture pipes for conditions, assignments, `$()` and `@()`.
Keep statement-level error handling with resume-at-next-statement, rethrowing flow-control signals untouched.
Match `try/catch/finally` semantics: typed handlers in order, `$_` bound to an `ErrorRecord`, `finally` runs after `return`, cleanup runs even for a stopped pipeline.
`switch` evaluates every clause per item; `foreach` wraps a non-enumerable in a one-element sequence; loop labels match case-insensitively with an empty label matching any loop.
Cache parsed script blocks by (file, text) but share only immutable compiled data between clones. Why: PowerShell clears the whole cache at 1024 entries; use an LRU instead.
Do not run an AMSI scan, suspicious-pattern hashing or admin-block checks as part of compilation in MicroteamShell; add a separate policy hook if needed.
Implement the enumeration rule and one-level unrolling exactly as in §7.1, including `AutomationNull`, strings and dictionaries as non-enumerated.
Arithmetic: wider-type promotion, `int` overflow to `double`, exact `int/int` stays `int`, zero division errors.
Collections on the left of comparison, `-like` and `-match` filter; scalar `-match` sets `$Matches`.
Implement `op_*` user-defined operators only for MicroteamShell's own types. Why: avoids reflection over arbitrary .NET types; same observable behavior for supported types.

Add a regex match timeout and size limits for string/array repetition in every mode. Why: PowerShell caps repetition only in restricted mode and no regex timeout was found (`UNVERIFIED`); a personal shell should fail safely.
Build the CORE rows first, in the order tokenizer, parser, AST, evaluator, scopes, operators, commands/pipeline, flow control, errors.
Add the EXTENDED rows (classes, modules, providers) only after the CORE rows pass the corpus; treat DSC and workflow as absent. Why: same language core with far less surface.
Do not implement `workflow`/`parallel`/`sequence`/`inlinescript` or the reserved keywords `from`, `define`, `var`; reject them with the same kind of parse error.
Expose `Parse(text)` returning AST, tokens (with comments) and all errors, with error nodes for broken input, from day one.
Provide `Find/FindAll` over the AST and a pure "literal data" evaluator for manifests and configuration.
Do not build the PowerShell 2 compatible token API or the V2 token rewriting.
If completion is added, keep type inference side-effect free (no command execution, no CIM lookups). Why: same completion quality for the shell's own types without running code.

Replace DLR binders by explicit dispatch functions per operation (`Add(left, right)`, `Convert(value, type)`, `GetMember(target, name)`, `Index(target, args)`) with a small per-site cache only if profiling shows a need. Why: the DLR is a mechanism, the observable behavior is the rule set.
Keep the dedicated helper operations (enumerate, to-object-array, write-to-pipe, array-assignment shaping, pipeline-result-to-bool); they encode language rules.
Do not port COM binders and `PSGetMemberBinder`'s COM/ETS-adapter paths in the first versions. Replace with a plain reflection member lookup.
Keep the five entry points (tokenize, parse, check, compile, invoke) as separate callable stages with narrow signatures so each can be tested alone.

Generate such graphs in CI from the shell's own sources to catch accidental coupling between stages. Why: the PowerShell graphs show the compiler calling parser-time helpers and the AST calling the compiler.
Use the search order of §7.1 with a per-(source,target) cache and an explicit rank for each outcome.
Convert strings to numbers with the same scanner as the tokenizer (hex, binary, suffixes, multipliers) and numbers to strings with invariant formatting (`G15`/`G7`, literal token text preserved).
Implement `IsTrue` exactly as in §7.3, including the one-element-list rule.

Support the language conversions (§7.1 step 8) and `Parse`/constructor/cast mechanisms for MicroteamShell's own types first; add reflection-based discovery of .NET `Parse`/`Create`/constructors only for the .NET types the shell exposes. Why: same observable casts for supported types without reflection over arbitrary assemblies.
Do not copy the Constrained-Language gate or the WDAC audit hook in the conversion layer; use an allow-list of target types at the shell's type-system boundary if a restricted mode is wanted.
Define behavior once, in the evaluator and the protocols, never per execution strategy; if two strategies are ever added, test them differentially.
`finally` must run for every exit (return, break, continue, throw) and flow-control signals must never be swallowed by catch-all handlers.

Do not port the typed arithmetic/comparison instruction families or the DLR-derived interpreter; they are unreachable or defective for PowerShell. Replace with the evaluator's own numeric semantics from [CONVERSION-RULES.md](CONVERSION-RULES.md).
Keep an oracle-recorded conformance corpus as the acceptance test of the new interpreter.
evidence: `test/powershell/Language/Parser/` (the repository's own language tests, see REFERENCE-TEST-CORPUS).

text: Keep one declaration per operator/keyword (spelling, kind, precedence, flags, evaluator) and generate the tables, instead of parallel arrays kept in sync by assertions. Why: same behavior, less drift.

Give every AST node one visitor interface with a default method; add a test that visits all nodes of a corpus with each visitor. Why: PowerShell's two-generation visitor scheme is only for compatibility.
Classify each new construct for restricted evaluation at the time it is added.

Build `S1`, a tree-walking evaluator that implements the protocols of IR-SPEC §5, as the first and only engine until measurements justify another tier. Why: same observable behavior as PowerShell's compiled pipeline with a fraction of the machinery.
If a second tier is added, test it differentially against the first on the whole corpus.
Do not adopt `Reflection.Emit` or `Expression.Compile` as the core engine.

A tree-walker over the AST can replace the IR, provided it implements the protocols in §5 (output pipe, `$?`, error-action resume, positions, flow control). Why: the observable behavior is defined by the protocols, not by expression trees.
Statements write to an output pipe; assignments, `++`/`--` and conditions do not; capturing output swaps the current pipe and restores it in a `finally`.
Wrap each statement so that non-flow-control exceptions go to the error-action policy and execution continues with the next statement when the policy says so.

Represent break/continue/return as control-flow signals inside the evaluator, and as exceptions only when crossing function or script-block boundaries. Why: PowerShell uses labels in-lambda and exceptions across lambdas; a tree-walker has no lambdas but still crosses script-block calls.
Keep a per-statement sequence-point index in the call frame so errors and the debugger can report positions.
Treat this specification plus the quirks catalog as the acceptance baseline and add oracle-confirmed tests per statement.
Keep the specification in the shell's repository as executable examples (snippet + expected result) rather than prose only. Why: same content, checkable.
Treat the command line as one script command followed by an output command in an ordinary pipeline, so interactive and file execution share a path.
Parse the whole text before running anything and report incomplete input distinctly so a REPL can ask for another line.
Run script blocks through a begin/process/end command processor that sets `$_`/`$input`, scopes, error pipe and language mode around each clause.

Merge the `CommandProcessor`/`DlrScriptCommandProcessor` split into one script command processor. Why: the split exists for cmdlet-style binding of advanced functions; the observable begin/process/end behavior is the same.
Use the precedence levels and left associativity above; keep the comma tighter than binary operators and put ternary and assignment below.
Choose the operation by the left operand's type and convert the right operand to it (CONVERSION-RULES); keep the `i`/`c` case variants and the array-filtering behavior of comparison operators.
Implement operators as ordinary functions with an explicit dispatch table instead of dynamic binding sites. Why: same observable results; no DLR.

Use the recorded oracle outputs as the expected values of the new interpreter's conformance suite and re-run the oracle for each new quirk. Why: same coverage with an automated diff instead of manual review.
Organize the new shell's specification tests by the same feature folders (parser, operators, scripting, classes) and keep one behavior per test.
Write the new suite in the shell's own language plus a small C# harness, so tests run without PowerShell. Why: same coverage, no dependency on the reference implementation.
Implement the seven-step error-action algorithm of §6.1 as one function used by the statement runner.
Use label-carrying break/continue signals where an empty label matches any loop.
Hashtable literal construction rejects null and duplicate keys; `+` of hashtables creates a new table and throws on a shared key.
Cap string and array repetition in all modes (not only data sections). Why: PowerShell caps only in restricted mode; a personal shell should not be able to exhaust memory by accident.
Do not port the class-method wrapper machinery (`ScriptBlockMemberMethodWrapper`, `SessionStateKeeper`, Reflection.Emit class definition) in the first versions; classes are EXTENDED scope.
Dynamic scoping for reads (walk to parents, skip `private`), local-only writes, explicit `script:`/`global:`/`local:`/`private:` qualifiers.
Each function/script-block call creates a child scope; dot-sourcing runs in the caller's scope; a script file is a script scope.
Type constraints on assignment (`[int]$x = …`) attach transformation/validation attributes to the variable and replace the previous ones on re-declaration.
Support `ReadOnly`, `Constant`, `Private`, `AllScope`, with the write rules of §7.1.
Keep one variable store per scope (no tuple slots) in the first implementation, but keep the lookup API narrow so slots can be added. Why: same observable behavior; slots are an optimization.
Strict-mode version is found by walking scopes, stopping at the module scope; version 0 means off.
Do not implement the untrusted-value marking tied to Constrained Language Mode unless a language-mode feature is adopted.
Make a script block a first-class value with an AST, a bound scope (optional), and a captured language mode (if any); share the parsed/compiled data between clones.
`GetNewClosure` snapshots the **current scope's** unrestricted variables by value into a private scope bound to the clone.
Provide `Invoke`, `InvokeReturnAsIs` (call operator semantics) and `InvokeWithContext` as separate entry points funneling into one invoke routine.
Implement closures without a module object: a scope object holding the snapshot. Why: same observable behavior; module objects are EXTENDED scope.
Omit steppable pipelines and the `PowerShell` object conversion (`GetPowerShell`) in the first versions.
Treat QRK-01 to QRK-27 and QRK-30 to QRK-32 as part of the baseline language and specify them with tests before implementing.
Keep the observable behavior of QRK-04, QRK-21 and QRK-22 with safer mechanisms (full scan, single comparer, caps in all modes).
Do not reproduce parse-time side effects (QRK-28, QRK-29) or tokenizer-level pragma handling (QRK-03).
Keep the six boundaries as explicit interfaces with the three error channels (diagnostics, runtime exception, error record).
Place static policy at B3, content policy at B4, and a single invoke/convert choke point at B5.
Pass tokenizer mode as an argument and keep annotations in a side model. Why: same behavior, removes hidden state.

Start with a tree-walking evaluator only; it is a valid first tier (all observable behavior is defined by the IR semantics, not by the JIT). `INFERENCE`: PowerShell's tiers are equivalent by design ([EQUIVALENCE-SPEC.md](EQUIVALENCE-SPEC.md)).

If a second tier is ever added, trigger it by call count with a deterministic (synchronous) policy first, and keep results independent of the tier. Why: PowerShell's asynchronous promotion makes tier choice nondeterministic.

Keep two variable-storage strategies visible in the design: fast slots when the scope is private and analyzable, dynamic lookup when debugging, dot-sourcing, or `AllScope`/`New-Variable`-style access is possible.

Do not copy background (thread-pool) compilation of hot loops with an in-place instruction replacement; it needs the interpreter and compiled code to share frames exactly. Replace by an explicit, synchronous optimization step if a loop optimizer is wanted.
Keep the exit-code rule and the specific codes (0, 1, 64, 70, 149) so automation behaves the same.
Four-profile order and per-profile fault isolation; `-NoProfile` skips all.
Keep line editing external, but define a small editor interface (read line with completion and history) instead of loading a module by name.
Separate the executable into a thin launcher and a library that exposes `Start(args)` and `Start(initialSessionState, args)` like `ConsoleShell`.

Apply policy (lockdown, language mode, allowed switches) from a signed policy source before parsing switches that widen access, and refuse to start server modes without an authenticated transport. DEV: DEV-HOST-200.
Do not carry the Windows-only pieces (`ConsoleControl` Win32 calls, jump list, `-windowstyle`, `-sta` by default, Hyper-V socket modes) into the first version. DEV: DEV-HOST-201.
Keep the three-level host contract (host, UI, raw UI) and the lifecycle notifications; host authors depend on them.
Replace exception-based capability probing with explicit capability flags on the host (supports raw UI, VT, interactive session, debugger).
Nested prompts and debugger prompts run at the strictest language mode seen.
Provide a headless default host and typed prompt results as part of the SDK so embedders do not subclass the full UI contract.
A restricted-session baseline factory (empty, no language, fail on open error).
A fluent command builder (command, script, parameter, statement) with sync, async and streaming-input invocation.
Add cancellation tokens and per-invocation time and memory budgets to the invoke API (the original has `Stop` only).
Make the default embedded session restricted and require an explicit opt-in to full language and unrestricted command visibility. DEV: DEV-SDK-205.
Publish a written compatibility contract that classifies changes and requires a protocol version bump for wire changes.
Ship a metapackage that pins transitive dependencies, but generate it from the build graph and publish reference assemblies for the public surface.
Keep one small native surface per OS with generated bindings and a layout check in CI, instead of hand-copied structs.
One file per native function, source-generated marshalling, `SafeHandle` for owned handles, UTF-16 on Windows and UTF-8 on Unix.
Pick one interop style (source-generated) and one `bool` marshalling convention per class; do not let three generations coexist.
Native library resolution must prefer the application directory and a signed or pinned per-RID folder, and refuse writable locations unless a policy allows them. DEV: DEV-PLAT-232.

Isolate OS differences behind one platform interface (paths, process launch, links, console, logging, identity) with a runtime capability table, and keep conditional compilation for the interface implementations only.
Honour XDG directories on Unix and known folders on Windows, create on demand, and report (not hide) a failure to create them.
Define the security-zone and execution-policy concept for every OS the shell supports, or declare it unsupported through one status API. DEV: DEV-PLAT-233.
Replace unsynchronized static caches for lazily resolved OS data with a concurrent map or a per-call lookup.
Treat CIM/WMI as an optional adapter module, not part of the base command set.
Leave OS-specific diagnostics out of the initial command set and offer them as optional modules.
Keep path- and item-commands provider-agnostic (the same verb set for files, registry, environment, functions) and let providers declare capabilities.
Route OS-level actions (process, service, computer) through an explicit capability so they can be denied per policy.
Split the utility set by risk: pure data/formatting commands vs code-loading (`Add-Type`, `Invoke-Expression`) and network commands, so a policy can grant them independently.
Implement object-manipulation commands against the public cmdlet base-class API only, so third-party modules can replace them.
Keep transcription as a host service behind a command pair, so non-console hosts can supply their own sink.
Use the platform's standard structured-logging/ETW abstractions (`EventSource`, OpenTelemetry) instead of a private ETW wrapper.
Keep GUI helpers behind a late-bound host service (reflection or plug-in) so the engine never references UI assemblies.
Expose signature validation and policy queries as ordinary commands over a policy service so audit tooling can use the same API as users.
Do not rely on `SecureString` cmdlets as a secrets boundary; replace with an OS-keychain-backed secret type (see Phase 5 blueprint).
Do not carry the WSMan command family into the new shell; remoting transport should be pluggable behind one session abstraction.
Register built-in commands from a declarative table (name -> implementing type -> help) as PowerShell does, but generate the table from attributes at build time so it cannot drift from the classes.
Keep `ForEach-Object`/`Where-Object` as engine-level commands with direct pipeline access so script-block pipelines do not pay module-load or binding overhead.
